evidence.quote: producing products or services that are targeted to consumers who are residents of the state

summary.short: Iowa statute (Senate File 262; Iowa Code ch. 715D) giving Iowa residents consumer rights over personal data and imposing duties on controllers and processors, enforced by the Attorney General; effective 1 January 2025.
summary.long: Iowa Senate File 262 (Iowa Code ch. 715D) regulates personal data of Iowa residents acting in an individual or household context. It covers persons doing business in Iowa or targeting Iowa residents that control or process personal data of at least 100,000 consumers in a calendar year, or 25,000 consumers while deriving over 50% of gross revenue from sale of personal data. Excluded are the state, financial institutions, nonprofits, higher education institutions, and certain health, credit and other data. Consumers may access, delete, port and opt out of sale of their data; controllers must respond within 90 days, extendable by 45 days, and offer an appeal. Controllers must maintain data security practices, give notice and an opt-out before processing sensitive data for nonexempt purposes, avoid discrimination for exercising rights, publish a privacy notice and disclose sales and targeted advertising. Processors must assist controllers under specified contract terms. The Attorney General has exclusive enforcement power, must give 90 days' notice and an opportunity to cure, and may seek injunctions and civil penalties up to $7,500 per violation. No private right of action exists. Local laws on personal data processing are preempted. Effective 1 January 2025.

thresholds.variable_text: age of a natural person defined as a child
thresholds.value_text: younger than thirteen years of age
thresholds.consequence: Defines child. Parent or guardian may invoke consumer rights for a known child (Sec. 3(1)), and personal data collected from a known child is a sensitive data category (Sec. 1(26)(c)).

evidence.quote: “Child” means any natural person younger than thirteen years of age.

thresholds.variable_text: radius of location precision for precise geolocation data
thresholds.value_text: within a radius of one thousand seven hundred fifty feet
thresholds.measurement: precision and accuracy of location data derived from technology, expressed as a radius
thresholds.consequence: Location data at this precision is precise geolocation data, a sensitive data category (Sec. 1(26)(d)).
thresholds.conditions: Data identifies the specific location of a natural person with precision and accuracy within the stated radius; excludes content of communications and utility metering data (Sec. 1(19)).

evidence.quote: identifies the specific location of a natural person with precision and accuracy within a radius of one thousand seven hundred fifty feet.

thresholds.variable_text: ownership or voting share for control in the definition of affiliate
thresholds.value_text: more than fifty percent of the outstanding shares of any class of voting security
thresholds.measurement: outstanding shares of any class of voting security of a company
thresholds.consequence: Ownership above this level is one form of control used to define affiliate (Sec. 1(1)), which is referenced in the sale exclusion (Sec. 1(25)(c)) and the third party definition (Sec. 1(29)).
thresholds.conditions: Other control prongs in Sec. 1(1)(b) and (c) are alternatives; affiliate also includes entities under common control or sharing common branding.

evidence.quote: Ownership of, or the power to vote, more than fifty percent of the outstanding shares of any class of voting security of a company.

thresholds.variable_text: number of consumer requests per consumer per year for which information is provided free of charge
thresholds.value_text: up to twice annually per consumer
thresholds.consequence: Information in response to a consumer request is provided free of charge up to this frequency. The text states no separate fee rule for requests beyond this number.
thresholds.conditions: Fee permitted only for manifestly unfounded, excessive, repetitive, technically unfeasible requests or where the primary purpose is not exercising a consumer right (Sec. 3(2)(c)).

evidence.quote: Information provided in response to a consumer request shall be provided by a controller free of charge, up to twice annually per consumer.
